title: They liked you more than you think.
body: After a conversation, people consistently underestimate how much the other person liked them and enjoyed it. Psychologists call it the liking gap. Your small message probably landed better than you fear.
cite: Boothby, Cooney, Sandstrom & Clark, Psychological Science, 2018

title: Friendship is built in hours.
body: One study found it takes about 50 hours together to go from acquaintance to casual friend, and more than 200 to become close friends. Every coffee, walk and call is a real deposit.
cite: Hall, Journal of Social and Personal Relationships, 2018

title: Voices connect.
body: People expect a call to feel awkward, but hearing someone's voice creates a stronger bond than text, and it's rarely as awkward as they feared.
cite: Kumar & Epley, Journal of Experimental Psychology: General, 2021

title: Appreciation lands harder than you think.
body: People who express gratitude underestimate how happy it will make the other person, and overestimate how awkward it will feel.

title: Awe makes worries smaller.
body: Moments of awe, like vast views, night skies or big music, shrink the sense of self, ease rumination and make people more generous.

title: Picture your best possible self.
body: Writing for a few minutes about a future where things went well lifts mood and optimism, and makes your goals feel more real.
cite: King, Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin, 2001

title: Plans beat willpower.
body: Deciding exactly when and where you'll do something (“At 7 pm at my desk, I will…”) makes you far more likely to follow through.

title: Talk to yourself like a friend.
body: Treating yourself with the kindness you'd offer a friend is linked to less anxiety and more resilience. It doesn't make you lazy; it makes you more likely to try again.
